title: I was... wrong? (Giving Mike Israetel a Fair Review of RP's Mass Gain Training
summary: After admitting the previous review was of a fake Israetel program, NH reviews the AM/PM six-day split Mike Israetel ran in RP's Mass Gain series. He praises the exercise selection and the arm days, but argues that for naturals it uses too much volume, too many machines and isolations as openers, too-high rep ranges, no hip hinges and an AM/PM structure that is unnecessary except on leg days. He consolidates sessions into single, shorter workouts.
claims: He will not delete his flawed review because hiding mistakes is cowardly and the video still helps people
AM/PM splits double daily volume and frequency interactions, which makes them very hard to program
The way influencers train is usually the way they teach, so their own training is fair to review
Naturals should open the day with a heavy compound when freshest, not an isolation
Five-rep machine flyes risk pec tendon injury; 8-15 is safer
Machines are all or nothing: a great machine can beat a barbell, a bad one injures you; check it, or use a Smith machine or barbell
Chest responds well to lower reps, 5-10 or 6-10, but so do other muscles
Train the upper back through a full stretch letting the shoulder blades protract; short jerky reps mostly train arms
In AM/PM training, keep the morning session less tiring or you will skip the evening one
JM-style Smith skull crushers mostly hit the triceps lateral head; flexing the shoulder more (French press) biases the long head
He prefers 8-12 reps close to failure over 10-20, though bodyweight moves like dips can go higher
Combine AM and PM sessions into one to save time: no second warm-up, travel or gym visit; time is your most important resource
Opening a leg day with leg curls works for Israetel because his knee-flexion machines have almost no hip hinge component; for normal squatters, hamstring work first limits the squat
On a leg day only heavy knee flexion or hip hinges justify opening the session; keep isolation for the end
High-rep squats can be limited by cardio or lactic acid pump before the muscle truly fails: artificial vs organic failure
He can curl 135 lb for 8 reps but cannot do 40 reps with an empty bar, showing high-rep fatigue is a different, less effective failure
Bodyweight walking lunges as finishers are mostly pump; to cause damage, weight them
The lower back exists to be used for hinges and knee flexions; babying it is only justified if you need it the next day
Schedule hard lower-body work in the morning and fun arm work in the afternoon, so the unpleasant session is not skipped
Spider curls are not preacher curls: the shoulders can move, making full extension safe for the biceps
Wide rep ranges like 10-20 only make sense with many sets (e.g. 5), where reps naturally drop set to set
Naturals rarely recover from heavy presses in 24 hours, so extra delt work the next day is a quirk of enhanced training
Direct forearm work is needed; Israetel's flexible exercise selection is his best trait
Enhanced bodybuilders use pulldowns because they are too heavy for pull-ups; if you can, do pull-ups
Naturals should skew toward compounds; a 70/30 isolation-to-compound ratio as here is typical of pros but wrong for naturals
Unsupported barbell rows train the whole posterior chain, not just lats
Training only above 10 reps gives less intense, lower-quality tonnage; 3-6 and 4-8 rep work also builds muscle and prevents plateaus
Rotate pulldown grips (chin-up, neutral) and favour pullovers to stretch the ribcage
0-1 RIR on 10-20 rep sets is pointless; RIR is best used in shorter rep ranges to avoid form breakdown
Mind-muscle connection that reduces intensity or makes you zone out on long sets wastes time
Natural lifters will not recover from presses in the morning plus heavy delt drop sets in the afternoon
Pick two knee-flexion and two hip-hinge variations and rotate them, opening alternate leg days with a different one
Lying on the floor after leg work is mostly theatre: pump and lactic acid do not mark relevant work
Training legs only twice a week with huge volume is worse than training them every two days
Volume must be judged across the whole week; high frequency forces lower per-session volume
The upper back recovers well from extra volume because it relies little on tendons and structure
A back day should open with a heavy row (supported or not) or heavy pull-up, not machines
Machines have a good stimulus-to-fatigue ratio but fatiguing the lower back also trains glutes and hamstrings; the plan lacks hip hinges and pulls from the floor
If you have a pencil neck, train the neck directly; it costs nothing
Eight sets of 10-20 light lateral raises is junk volume; the middle ground between Mentzer and maximal volume is where naturals grow
Trade two or three isolations for one compound to make a program more compact
AM/PM is only justified on leg days; the program lacks triceps long head, neck, calves and abs work
exercises: isolation opener only justified by AM/PM context
bodyweight version is just a pump
